channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy on pain intensity and functional disability in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (N unspecified) found that radial extracorporeal shockwave therapy (rESWT) significantly reduced pain (SMD = -0.72) in chronic low back pain, but functional disability improvement (MD = -6.12) did not reach clinical significance. Most outcomes were evaluated immediately post-intervention.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical activity guidelines' impact on cognition in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 RCTs (N=462) found that meeting physical activity guidelines for multiple sclerosis (PAG-MS) significantly improved processing speed (SMD = 0.29), visuospatial memory (SMD = 0.47), and verbal memory (SMD = 0.75) in individuals with MS.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Early supervised physiotherapy session-completion adherence and outcomes after acute lateral ankle sprain in professional athletes: concurrent indirect associations through kinesiophobia
item.description: A single-center retrospective cohort study (N=118 professional athletes) found that higher adherence to early supervised physiotherapy (per 10-percentage-point increase) was associated with a higher rate of achieving return to sport (HR = 1.27), lower odds of ankle instability (OR = 0.70), and lower residual pain (B = -0.36) after acute lateral ankle sprain. Kinesiophobia was identified as an important concurrent psychological correlate.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found that treadmill exercise with vertical traction and partial body weight support (VT+TE) yielded greater improvements in gait, disability, and trunk repositioning compared to treadmill exercise alone (TE) or core stabilization in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A 4-year prospective cohort study found that the majority of older adults with massive irreparable rotator cuff tears responded well to nonoperative treatment, with significant improvements in shoulder function and pain persisting long-term. Longer symptom duration, smoking, and diabetes were associated with worse outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found that both sensory electrical stimulation (SES) and alternating EMG-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG), when added to conventional physical therapy, significantly improved upper-limb motor function in chronic stroke patients, with no significant difference between the two stimulation methods.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of short-foot and toe-curl exercises on movement control during single-leg landing after ACL reconstruction: An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
item.description: In an exploratory RCT (N=38 ACLR patients), short-foot exercise (SFE) lowered hip adduction excursion during single-leg landing at 6 weeks compared to toe-curl exercise (TCE), with a between-group difference of -6.30° (95% CI, -9.19 to -3.41; ES, -1.41), and this improvement was maintained at 12 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A mobile-based multimodal monitoring system with clinician feedback for home rehabilitation after stroke: a randomized clinical trial
item.description: In a single-center RCT with 110 stroke survivors, a 6-week multimodal monitoring intervention significantly improved 6-minute walk distance by 23.15m (95% CI 6.70 to 39.60; p=0.006) and balance compared to standard care, with high participant satisfaction but mean adherence of 60%.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Efficacy of Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation (NMES) on Lower Limb Mobility and Activities of Daily Living in Post-Stroke Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (579 patients) found that neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) significantly improved Fugl-Meyer Assessment (MD=3.40, P=0.001), ankle dorsiflexion ROM (MD=1.56, P=0.04), TUG (MD=-1.96, P=0.03), BBS (MD=10.78, P=0.005), PASS (MD=5.05, P<0.00001), and MBI (MD=13.29, P=0.02) in post-stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Construct validity and intrasession intra-rater reliability of the stair and step tests in individuals with multiple sclerosis.
item.description: This study involving 100 MS patients found the Stair and Step Tests have excellent test-retest reliability (ICC 0.997 and 0.955, respectively) and strong construct validity, making them practical for monitoring mobility.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Clinical and functional outcomes of aquatic plyometrics in adolescent patellofemoral pain syndrome: a dual-arm randomized controlled trial | Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine
item.description: A dual-arm randomized controlled trial (n=56) found that aquatic plyometric exercises significantly reduced pain (p=0.004, η²p=0.14) and improved quadriceps and hamstring peak torque (e.g., quadriceps 120°/s: p=0.006, η²p=0.13) compared to conventional exercises in adolescents with patellofemoral pain syndrome.
item.author: J Rehabil Med

item.title: Effects of different types of exercise in patients with stroke: a network meta-analysis
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 52 RCTs (n=2,329) on stroke rehabilitation found whole-body vibration most beneficial for balance (BBS: MD 9.86, 95% CrI 4.78-14.92) with moderate certainty evidence. Aerobic, aerobic+strength, coordinative, and strength training improved walking endurance, but evidence for gait performance, functional mobility, ADL, and lower-extremity motor recovery was less robust or limited.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Measurement properties of observational gait analysis tools in neurological disorders: a COSMIN meta-analysis.
item.description: A COSMIN systematic review and meta-analysis of 28 articles found no observational gait analysis tool was fully recommended for use in neurological populations, but the Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS) and Gait Assessment and Intervention Tool (G.A.I.T.) showed the best potential for recommendation in stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Remote Ischemic Conditioning Modulates Spinal Reflex Excitability in Healthy Young Adults: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: A pilot RCT involving 26 healthy young adults randomized to RIC or sham groups found that remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) paired with balance training led to a greater reduction in Hslp/Mslp ratio (p=0.02) and improved balance performance (p=0.02) compared to sham, suggesting RIC may modulate spinal reflex excitability and enhance neuroplastic adaptations.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: What are the barriers and facilitators to engagement with physiotherapy among women experiencing adverse effects associated with menopause?
item.description: A qualitative study of 12 women in the UK identified fatigue, cognitive issues, low self-efficacy, and negative language from healthcare professionals as barriers to physiotherapy engagement for menopause-related musculoskeletal pain, while direct inquiry about menopause, individualized treatment, and education were facilitators.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Delivering a high-dose walking booster program after stroke: a multimethod study of therapists' beliefs and experiences nested within a randomized trial.
item.description: A multimethod study explored intervention therapists' beliefs and experiences delivering a high-dose walking booster program (HiWalk) to stroke survivors more than 6 months post-stroke, identifying facilitators like training and team support, and barriers such as beliefs about survivor capability and resource limitations.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Early postoperative functional exercise adherence and its association with 3-month hip functional recovery among older adults after femoral neck fracture surgery: a prospective observational study.
item.description: A prospective observational study of 230 older adults after femoral neck fracture surgery found moderate early postoperative functional exercise adherence before discharge, negatively correlated with kinesiophobia and pain, and positively with self-efficacy and social support. Higher adherence was positively associated with 3-month hip functional recovery (Harris Hip Score).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Barriers and Facilitators Influencing Physiotherapists' Adherence to Clinical Practice Guidelines and Return to Sport Criteria after Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: A Qualitative Study in Austria.
item.description: A qualitative study identified limited usability of ACLR guidelines, patient expectations, professional attitudes, and interprofessional misalignment as key barriers to CPG and RTS criteria adherence among Austrian physiotherapists.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Preoperative factors associated with quadriceps strength 1 year after total knee arthroplasty: a prospective longitudinal study.
item.description: In 39 older adults with uncomplicated recovery after TKA, preoperative normalized quadriceps strength (B = 0.72, p < 0.001) and limb symmetry index (LSI) (B = -0.17, p = 0.013) were significantly associated with quadriceps strength 1 year post-TKA, suggesting higher preoperative strength and LSI predict better 1-year outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Do treatment parameters of dry needling influence its effect on pain? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 71 comparisons found no dose-response relationship between dry needling parameters (sessions, muscles, local twitch responses) and neck pain effectiveness (QM = 0.26, p = 0.968 to QM = 3.17, p = 0.205) due to high heterogeneity and incomplete reporting.
item.author: PubMed
